# Forge contributor instructions

- v1 is Android and iOS only. DevExpress MAUI does not render on Windows or Mac Catalyst; it compiles against a stub and crashes at runtime.
- DevExpress registration calls must follow `.UseMauiApp<App>()`; analyzer DXM001 enforces this order.
- Use `dx:RadialProgressBar` for rings, not `dx:RadialGauge`. There is no `dx:RangeBar`.
- `Forge.Domain` and `Forge.Core` must not reference MAUI or DevExpress; FORGE001 enforces this.
- Never name a namespace `Application` or `Theme` under the `Forge` root because they shadow framework types and a global using alias does not fix it.
- Features register themselves via `Add<Name>Feature`; EF entities use `IEntityTypeConfiguration` discovered from the assembly. Do not edit `MauiProgram.cs` or `ForgeDbContext` for feature work.
- Reach the database only through `IDataSessionFactory`: `await using var session = sessions.Create();` then `session.Repository<T>()` and `session.SaveChangesAsync(ct)`. Never register or resolve `IRepository<>`/`IUnitOfWork` from DI and never `new EfRepository`/`EfUnitOfWork` in feature code — separately resolved instances get their own `DbContext`, so the save commits nothing and the writes are lost silently. `Test-DataAccessPatterns.ps1` enforces this.
- Don't run `dotnet ef migrations add` on a feature branch. Migration files and `ForgeDbContextModelSnapshot.cs` are whole-file generated artefacts that git cannot merge, so two branches scaffolding at once means redoing the work. Change entities and configurations, write the schema delta into a short doc, and the migration is generated once at integration. See `docs/persistence/migrations.md`.
- A new non-nullable `Guid UserProfileId` defaults to `Guid.Empty` on existing rows, and `ProfileScope` is fail-closed, so those rows become invisible rather than merely unowned. Any migration adding an owner column must backfill it, or a user upgrades into an empty history.
- XAML colour comes from DevExpress semantic roles, and sizes come from `ForgeTokens.xaml`; avoid hex literals and magic numbers.
- Never host caller content in a `ContentPresenter` outside a `ControlTemplate`. It deliberately opts out of binding-context inheritance, so every child `{Binding}` silently resolves against null and renders blank. Use a plain `ContentView`. This cost 98 dead bindings across 16 pages in `ForgeCard`, invisible to builds and tests because a failed `IsVisible` binding falls back to `true`.
- Local data is encrypted with SQLCipher, which requires `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite.Core` plus an explicit `SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlcipher` reference. Never use the plain `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` package: it drags in the stock SQLite bundle, and `PRAGMA key` against stock SQLite is an unknown pragma that SQLite ignores without error — so the database ships plaintext while every claim about encryption stays in the privacy policy and the store declarations. This shipped once. See `docs/security/database-encryption.md`.
- When verifying anything that changes a package reference on Android, deploy with `-p:EmbedAssembliesIntoApk=true`. Debug Fast Deployment keeps managed assemblies in `files/.__override__/` on the device and leaves stale ones behind, so the app runs a mixture of two builds and the result means nothing.
- Add `SemanticProperties.Description` to interactive controls. DevExpress buttons are otherwise exposed to Android's accessibility tree as non-focusable text with no description, so screen readers cannot reach them.
- A clean build and a green test suite do not mean the app runs. Six shipped defects were visible only on a device: DI activation, theme init order, seed deserialization, a startup race, accessibility exposure, and the `ContentPresenter` binding trap. Verify UI work on an emulator.
- Tests use xUnit v3 with Shouldly. Do not introduce FluentAssertions.
- CI runs `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` over all six projects. A clean build does not mean a clean format gate, so run it before pushing or CI will fail on whitespace alone.
